### Setup
```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(here)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the CSV file
df <- readr::read_delim(
  here("data", "df_for_stepwise_regression.csv"),
  delim = ","
)
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# We define the target variable name
target_variable <- "GPP_NT_VUT_REF"

# We define potential predictor variable names, we exclude identifiers, timestamp, and the target itself
potential_predictors <- setdiff(names(df), c("siteid", "TIMESTAMP", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF"))

# We keep only numeric predictors 
numeric_predictors <- names(which(sapply(df[, potential_predictors], is.numeric)))
potential_predictors <- numeric_predictors 

# We create a subset of the dataframe with only the target and potential predictors
df_subset <- df[, c(target_variable, potential_predictors)]
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# We remove any row that has at least a NA
df_clean <- na.omit(df_subset)

# Check dimensions after removing NAs
print(paste("Original dimensions:", dim(df)[1], "rows"))
print(paste("Dimensions after NA removal:", dim(df_clean)[1], "rows"))
```


### Stepwise forward regression algorithm implementation
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# We initialize lists to keep track of predictors
selected_predictors <- c() # Start with an empty set of selected predictors
remaining_predictors <- potential_predictors # Start with all potential predictors as remaining

# Initialize variables to track the best model found so far
# We start with the intercept-only model as the 'best' initially
best_model_formula <- as.formula(paste(target_variable, "~ 1")) 
initial_model <- lm(best_model_formula, data = df_clean)
best_model_aic <- AIC(initial_model) # AIC of the intercept-only model
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# best_model_aic holds the AIC of our current best model 
# selected_predictors holds the predictors in the current best model
# remaining_predictors holds the predictors still left to try

while (length(remaining_predictors) > 0) {

  ############### We try adding one predictor (inner loop), 1 predictor per round ###############
  best_aic_this_iteration <- Inf 
  predictor_to_add_this_iteration <- NULL 
  

  for (predictor in remaining_predictors) { # We a predictor 
    
    # We make a temporary model to test each predictor
    current_predictors_try <- c(selected_predictors, predictor)
    formula_str <- paste(target_variable, "~", paste(current_predictors_try, collapse = " + "))
    current_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)
    
    # We evaluate the temporary model with AIC, we use tryCactch to handle error in case of collinearity
    current_model <- tryCatch({ lm(current_formula, data = df_clean) }, error = function(e) { NULL })
    
    if (!is.null(current_model)) {
        current_aic <- AIC(current_model) 
        
        # We compare the AIC of the temporary model with the best AIC so far 
        if (current_aic < best_aic_this_iteration) {
            best_aic_this_iteration <- current_aic # Retains the new AIC if it is smaller
            predictor_to_add_this_iteration <- predictor # Add the new predictor into the list of predictors if it improves the AIC
        }
    }
  }  # end of the inner loop

  ###################### Comparaison with best model #################################
  
  # We check if in this round we found a better AIC (and a better model) compared to the previous best result
  if (best_aic_this_iteration < best_model_aic) {
    
    
    # Yes, update our best model
    best_model_aic <- best_aic_this_iteration 
    selected_predictors <- c(selected_predictors, predictor_to_add_this_iteration) 
    remaining_predictors <- setdiff(remaining_predictors, predictor_to_add_this_iteration) # Remove predictor already tested
    best_model_formula <- as.formula(paste(target_variable, "~", paste(selected_predictors, collapse = " + ")))
    
    # The while loop starts again in order to test a new predictor
    
  } else {
    # No, adding the best remaining predictor didn't improve the AIC
    break # Stop the whole process and we exit the 'while' loop
  } 
    
} # End of the main 'while' loop

# --- Final Results of Selection ---
cat("\n--- Stepwise forward selection finished ---\n")
print(paste("Selected predictors:", paste(selected_predictors, collapse = ", ")))
print(paste("Final model formula:", deparse(best_model_formula))) # deparse handles formula object nicely
print(paste("Final model AIC:", round(best_model_aic, 2)))
```


### Final model fitting and result visualization
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} 
# We fit the final linear model using the formula decided by the stepwise process
final_model <- lm(best_model_formula, data = df_clean)

print(summary(final_model)) 

# We add predictions as a new column to the dataframe and we use the final model to calculate the predicted GPP values
df_clean$predicted_GPP <- predict(final_model, newdata = df_clean)

# We create the scatter plot
plot_gpp <- ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = .data[[target_variable]], y = predicted_GPP)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) + 
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs. Predicted GPP",
    subtitle = paste("Stepwise forward regression model (Final AIC =", round(best_model_aic, 2), ")"),
    x = "Observed GPP (GPP_NT_VUT_REF)", 
    y = "Predicted GPP"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Print the plot to display it in the R Markdown output
print(plot_gpp) 

################ Calculate Final RMSE ###########################
# Calculate residuals (actual - predicted)
residuals_final <- df_clean[[target_variable]] - df_clean$predicted_GPP
# Calculate RMSE
rmse_final <- sqrt(mean(residuals_final^2))
print(paste("Final model root mean squared error (RMSE):", round(rmse_final, 3)))
```
